claims.text: On the document Fouche calls the SAC-DARPA Classified Document: 'This letter is UNCLASSIFIED. It was never marked as classified material (no classification markings, no control number, no Copy X of Y). There is nothing unusual about the letterhead. Use of the DoD seal is standard. The letter was signed by the NCO in Charge, Airman Aircraft Maintenance Assignments Section, Office of the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel... Where it says REPLY TO: DARPA, this might be a five-letter office code (such as DPAQR, the Command Records Branch at SAC HQ). This letter simply indicates that the Air Force Manpower and Personnel Center (AFMPC) has approved an After Action Review (or Report)'. The page image opened by this research corroborates the absence of any classification marking and the signature block he describes.

claims.text: On what Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center is, in his own published reference work: 'Since the late 1970s, the Groom Lake facility has been operated by Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center (DET 3 AFFTC) under Air Force Systems Command (AFSC) and later Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC).' This is the statement that gives Fouche's AF Form 77a of 24 August 1979 its meaning.

conflicts: Merlin's gloss of AAR as 'After Action Review (or Report)' was not verified against any Air Force instruction opened by this research, and neither his reading nor Fouche's 'After Action Request' is settled here. His reading of 'REPLY TO: DARPA' as a five-letter office code is separately and directly corroborated by the artefact's own signature block, which places the originating office inside the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel, and not inside any research agency.

label: Peter W. Merlin
narrative: Peter W. Merlin is on this board because he is the rare thing this subject almost never produces: a named, credentialed, checkable analyst who has gone through a claimant's own documents item by item. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Studies from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, has researched Area 51 since 1984, co-founded the X-Hunters Aerospace Archeology Team, and has written or co-written nine books, three of them published by NASA and the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. His four findings against Fouche are not opinion: each is a falsifiable specific about something outside Fouche's own testimony. He says the 'SAC-DARPA' letter carries no classification marking, which the page image corroborates. He says the aircraft Fouche captioned 'Have Blue' is the first YF-117A SENIOR TREND prototype. He says no person called Steve Stenson was ever commander of the Air Force Flight Test Center. He says the KGB props are fakes sold in surplus stores. He has not, so far as any opened record shows, been checked and found wrong. The reason he earns a node rather than a footnote is that he is on both sides of the same file: his own published reference work on Groom Lake is what identifies Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center as the unit operating the airfield, and that identification is the only thing that makes Fouche's single best document mean anything at all.
